# 野田竜之介（Ryunosuke Noda）

腎臓内科医・医療AI研究者。聖マリアンナ医科大学 腎臓・高血圧内科 助教、博士（医学）。特定非営利活動法人 日本医療AIリテラシー協会（JAMAIL）理事長として、医療AIの学びの公共基盤づくりにも取り組んでいる。

---

## Statement — AIは医療と医師をどう変えるのか

腎臓内科医として診療を行いながら、機械の知性を測ってきた。医学の問いに、AIはどこまで答えられるのか。血液と尿検査の数値から、病をどこまで言い当てられるのか。測るほどに、問いは反転していった。—着目すべきは、機械ではなく、医師の側ではないか。

同じAIを前にして、強くなっていく医師と、衰えていく医師がいる。その分かれ目で、医療の未来が変わるかもしれない。だから、臨床現場に立ち続ける。研究で確かめる。学びの場を、誰にでも開かれた公共財として築く。

AIによって医療は、医師は、どうなっていくのか。その答えを、当事者として見届けたい。

## Practice

- **診る（CLINICIAN）** — 全ての問いは、診療現場から始まる。腎臓内科医として診療所から大学病院まで、AIが医療に入っていく現場を見続ける。
- **測る（RESEARCHER）** — 機械の知性を、医学の問いで測る。生成AIの腎臓領域での性能検証や、腎疾患の診断・予後予測を行うAIの開発に取り組む。
- **開く（EDUCATOR）** — 医療AIの学びを、無償で誰にでも。特定非営利活動法人 日本医療AIリテラシー協会の理事長として、学びの公共基盤を育てる。

## Biography

- **2016** 筑波大学医学群卒業。医師免許取得。
- **2018** 東京新宿メディカルセンター、虎の門病院、日本赤十字社医療センターで専門研修。
- **2021** 聖マリアンナ医科大学大学院に進学。医療AI研究を開始。
- **2023** AcademiX Medicalを創設。
- **2025** 博士（医学）取得。聖マリアンナ医科大学 腎臓・高血圧内科 助教に就任。
- **2026** NPO法人日本医療AIリテラシー協会を設立、理事長に就任。

研究業績・講演・受賞の一覧は Portfolio、researchmap、CV（PDF）に。

## 業績（Portfolio）

正式・最新の業績一覧は researchmap（https://researchmap.jp/nodaryu）にあります。論文・学会発表は researchmap および各論文のDOIで照合できます。

### 研究の系譜（Research Narrative）

#### AIの医学の実力はどのくらいか（2023〜）

ChatGPTの登場直後から、腎臓内科の筆記試験問題を用いてAIの医学的な性能を測ってきた。ChatGPT・Bardの評価（*Clinical and Experimental Nephrology*, 2024, 筆頭・責任著者）を皮切りに、GPT-4による医師の意思決定支援（*Scientific Reports*, 2025, 筆頭・責任著者）、o1 proなど推論モデルの評価（*Frontiers in Medicine*, 2025, 筆頭・責任著者）、推論モデルと従来型のモデルの比較（*JMA Journal*, 2026, 最終・責任著者）へと評価系を発展させてきた。

#### AIは診断や予後を予測できるか（2024〜）

血液・尿検査という侵襲の少ないデータから腎疾患を診断予測するモデルを、自らコードを書いて開発してきた。IgA腎症の診断予測（*Scientific Reports*, 2024, 筆頭・責任著者）、微小変化型ネフローゼ症候群の診断予測（*Scientific Reports*, 2024, 筆頭・責任著者）を発表。現在は科研費（研究活動スタート支援・若手研究、いずれも研究代表者）により、汎用的な腎臓病診断予測モデルとIgA腎症の動的予後予測モデルの開発を進めている。

#### AIで医療はどうなっていくのか（2024〜）

研究で得た知見を、臨床医に届く言葉に変換する仕事をしている。総説論文として腎臓内科における人工知能の現状と展望（日本腎臓学会誌, 2024, 筆頭・責任著者）、医療者・AIエージェント・ロボットの三者協働による血液透析ケアの構想（*Clinical and Experimental Nephrology*, 2026, 筆頭・責任著者）を発表。2026年にはNPO法人日本医療AIリテラシー協会（JAMAIL）を設立した。現在は、「AIは医師の判断力・技能を強めるのか、衰えさせるのか」という問いを、研究として立ち上げている。

### 教育（Education）

2023年、医療AIを学ぶための完全無料のオンラインコミュニティ「AcademiX Medical」を有志と創設。オンライン勉強会、Slackでの情報共有を通じて、医療者と技術者が分野を越えて学び合う場を運営してきた。

2026年、この活動を持続可能な公共基盤とするため、特定非営利活動法人日本医療AIリテラシー協会（JAMAIL）を設立し、理事長に就任。医療AIに関する教育・人材育成、情報の発信、分野を越えた交流・連携の促進に取り組んでいる。（JAMAIL公式サイト: https://jamail.or.jp/）

# Ryunosuke Noda, MD, PhD

Ryunosuke Noda is a nephrologist, medical AI researcher, and educator based in Japan. He is an Assistant Professor in the Division of Nephrology and Hypertension at St. Marianna University School of Medicine, and the founding president of the Japanese Association for Medical AI Literacy (JAMAIL). His work spans clinical nephrology practice, research on the performance evaluation of generative AI in medicine and AI-based diagnosis and prognosis prediction of kidney disease, and free, open medical AI education.

## Statement

How will AI change medicine — and physicians?

As a nephrologist in daily practice, I have been measuring the intelligence of machines. How well can AI answer the questions of medicine? How accurately can it read disease from blood and urine tests? The more I measured, the more the question inverted itself — perhaps what deserves attention is not the machine, but the physician.

Before the same AI, some physicians will grow stronger while others will decline. On that divide, the future of medicine may turn. So I remain in clinical practice, verify through research, and build an open commons of learning for everyone.

How will medicine — and physicians — change with AI? I want to witness the answer as a participant.

## Practice

- **診る (CLINICIAN)** — Every question begins at the bedside. As a nephrologist practicing everywhere from neighborhood clinics to a university hospital, I keep watching the front line where AI enters medicine.
- **測る (RESEARCHER)** — Measuring machine intelligence with the questions of medicine — working on performance evaluation of generative AI in nephrology and development of AI for diagnosis and prognosis prediction of kidney disease.
- **開く (EDUCATOR)** — Opening medical AI education to everyone, free of charge. As founding president of the Japanese Association for Medical AI Literacy (JAMAIL), I cultivate a public foundation for learning.

## Biography

- **2016** — Graduated from the University of Tsukuba School of Medicine; licensed as a physician.
- **2018** — Clinical training at Tokyo Shinjuku Medical Center, Toranomon Hospital, and the Japanese Red Cross Medical Center.
- **2021** — Entered the graduate school of St. Marianna University School of Medicine; began research on medical AI.
- **2023** — Founded AcademiX Medical.
- **2025** — Received PhD (Medicine); appointed Assistant Professor, Division of Nephrology and Hypertension, St. Marianna University School of Medicine.
- **2026** — Established the Japanese Association for Medical AI Literacy (JAMAIL); appointed founding president.

Full lists of publications, lectures, and awards: Portfolio, researchmap (https://researchmap.jp/nodaryu), and the CV in English (PDF).

## Portfolio

The official, up-to-date list of achievements is on researchmap (https://researchmap.jp/nodaryu). Publications and presentations can be verified on researchmap and via each paper's DOI.

### Research Narrative

#### How capable is AI in medicine? (2023–)

Since immediately after ChatGPT's debut, I have been measuring the medical performance of AI using written examinations in nephrology. Starting with an evaluation of ChatGPT and Bard (*Clinical and Experimental Nephrology*, 2024; first & corresponding author), I have extended the evaluation framework to GPT-4's support of physician decision-making (*Scientific Reports*, 2025; first & corresponding author), the assessment of reasoning models such as o1 pro (*Frontiers in Medicine*, 2025; first & corresponding author), and a comparison of reasoning and conventional models (*JMA Journal*, 2026; last & corresponding author).

#### Can AI diagnose disease and predict outcomes? (2024–)

I have developed models that diagnose and predict kidney disease from minimally invasive blood and urine test data, writing the code myself. After publishing diagnostic prediction models for IgA nephropathy (*Scientific Reports*, 2024; first & corresponding author) and minimal change disease (*Scientific Reports*, 2024; first & corresponding author), I am now developing a generalizable diagnostic prediction model for kidney diseases and a dynamic prognostic model for IgA nephropathy, funded by JSPS KAKENHI grants (Research Activity Start-up and Early-Career Scientists; principal investigator of both).

#### Where is medicine going with AI? (2024–)

This is the work of translating research findings into words that reach practicing clinicians. I have published a review on the current status and prospects of artificial intelligence in nephrology (*Japanese Journal of Nephrology*, 2024; first & corresponding author) and a perspective on transforming hemodialysis care through tripartite collaboration among medical staff, AI agents, and robots (*Clinical and Experimental Nephrology*, 2026; first & corresponding author). In 2026, I established the Japanese Association for Medical AI Literacy (JAMAIL). I am now launching research on the question: does AI strengthen or weaken physicians' judgment and skills?

### Clinical Practice

From advanced acute care at a university hospital to primary care at community clinics and home-visit medicine. As a board-certified specialist in internal medicine, nephrology, and dialysis, I continue to practice on the front line.

- **2016** — Junior Resident, JCHO Tokyo Shinjuku Medical Center
- **2018** — Fellow, Internal Medicine / Nephrology, Toranomon Hospital
- **2019** — Fellow, Internal Medicine / Nephrology, JCHO Tokyo Shinjuku Medical Center
- **2020** — Staff Physician, Department of Nephrology, Japanese Red Cross Medical Center
- **2021** — Clinical Assistant, Division of Nephrology and Hypertension, St. Marianna University School of Medicine
- **2025** — Assistant Professor, Division of Nephrology and Hypertension, St. Marianna University School of Medicine (current)

### Education

In 2023, I co-founded AcademiX Medical, a completely free online community for learning medical AI. Through online study sessions and information sharing on Slack, it has become a place where medical professionals and engineers learn from one another across disciplines.

In 2026, to turn this activity into a sustainable public foundation, I established the Japanese Association for Medical AI Literacy (JAMAIL) and became its founding president — working on education and human resource development in medical AI, information sharing, and cross-disciplinary collaboration. (JAMAIL Official Site: https://jamail.or.jp/)
